text:
Still mild out there, running into the upper 60s this afternoon, a few degrees ahead of the forecast. A front is sliding through, so a few scattered showers will pass between about 5 and 7, right around the 4:36 sunset. Expect clouds more than color. Rain totals stay under a tenth of an inch, so a light jacket covers it. Things dry out by 9 and stay dry overnight. Clouds hang on, which keeps us mild, with a low around 50.

Tomorrow looks mostly dry. Morning and early afternoon should be partly sunny, with a high near 61, a little cooler than today. Showers could return by mid-afternoon, light and spotty. The models disagree on that, and the European one is much wetter than the others. I'd bet on a dry walk or ride before 3, then keep a hat or jacket handy. Saturday turns noticeably cooler, with highs only in the 40s to around 50.

Trending brighter and milder, partly sunny with a high near 56, and only a small chance of a stray shower after 1.
Veterans Day looks partly sunny and cool with a high near 50, a stray shower possible, and a cold night near 28.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-05T19:28:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Periods of scattered showers will continue this afternoon through the upcoming weekend as temperatures cool to near normal levels.
  2. There will be additional opportunities for non-impactful, beneficial precipitation during the early to middle portion of next week as the pattern remains unsettled.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 228 PM EST Thursday... No significant changes.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Isolated to scattered showers continue this afternoon into this evening as an initial cold front begins its passage through the region. Drier air directly behind the front will filter into northern New York and Vermont swiftly this evening, becoming enhanced by the of the right exit region of an incoming elongated jet streak, yielding dry conditions later this evening through the overnight period. However, with clouds slow to scour out due to lower-level moisture becoming trapped below a low- to mid-level inversion, temperatures will remain on the mild side. Expect lows in the low 40s to low 50s. Dry conditions remain steady through tomorrow morning and even early tomorrow afternoon as a secondary cold front and parent low are slow to make eastward progress off the Eastern Great Lakes. However, by mid-afternoon, isolated to scattered showers return, particularly for Lake-adjacent areas, the Adirondacks where upslope flow will overcome an overall lack of forcing, and along the VT/NH border as a low develops along today's initial cold front that looks to stall along the New England Coastline. Rainfall rates are anticipated to be light, with QPF generally remaining under 0.1" through tomorrow night. Tomorrow's highs will be a bit cooler than today, though still classify as above-normal with values in the low 50s to mid 60s. Lows tomorrow night will then largely be in the 40s with upper 30s across higher elevations. The passage of the secondary cold front tomorrow night will see temperatures fall much closer to normal than we have been over the last several days. Highs Saturday will only reach the 40s and 50s with additional chances for isolated to scattered showers across higher elevations as moist, cyclonic flow remains in place beneath an upper-level low moving into the Northeast. Lows Saturday night will then fall largely to the 30s and 40s with pockets of upper 20s across the Adirondacks and Greens. Sunday will remain seasonably chilly with additional potential for isolated, high-elevation showers, which could contain some snowflakes, and highs in the 30s to low 40s across higher elevations and upper 40s to low 50s in valley areas. Lows Sunday night will then fall largely to the 20s and 30s. KEY MESSAGE 2: Additional chances for precipitation come mostly for Monday and Wednesday next week as we remain in a more unsettled pattern. However, given the recent dry conditions, all precipitation will be beneficial and not pose any significant impacts. Temperatures will remain more consistently near normal next week with highs largely in the 40s and 50s and lows in the 20s and 30s.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Thursday! A round of rain showers looks to roll through from west to east this morning into the early afternoon. Another round of showers may pop up here and there through this evening and into the first part of tonight. Right now, it looks like we all see rain, but it’s not a ton with most only getting a couple tenths of an inch of new rain. Temperatures are a tad cooler with most in the low to mid-60s. Friday looks drier, but there could still be a spotty shower here and there. We continue to lose a little ground temperature-wise, as most areas talk high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s. The weekend could again feature a few showers for Saturday. Temperatures turn noticeably cooler with most only in the 40s to about 50 for Saturday afternoon. Sunday looks drier but could feature a spotty morning shower or two. Temperatures are generally stuck in the 40s for most. We’ll keep the clouds and a few spotty showers going into next week. There could even be a few mountain snowflakes from time-to-time Monday and Tuesday. While clouds and a few passing showers are present through the end of this week and into the upcoming weekend and to start next week, no one day looks to be a washout, and rain amounts top out at about 0.75″.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-04T21:02:00Z — same caveat): Showers Thursday morning taper to partial sun — Showers Thursday morning will taper through the afternoon, giving way to a partly sunny sky and temperatures reaching the 60s. A late evening or overnight thunderstorm cannot be ruled out in southern Vermont. The south breeze becomes a bit stronger, with gusts near 30 mph. Friday turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. A few hours of sunshine are likely, but New York will remain cloudier overall. Highs again reach the 60s. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with a few additional showers, especially on Saturday.
